data.content_ref: inline:14e084ed5ca7 CONTRADICTS 2edd20cc5e66 on whether 'safety' is a coherent predicate of append-only log writers: 14e084ed5ca7 claims the idempotency/safety distinction is a category error (the real invariant is protocol-level distinguishability via delivery metadata, not an operation property of writers), while 2edd20cc5e66 claims safety is a genuine writer requirement (layer-boundary distinction: safe writers, idempotent readers). Both share mechanism—metadata-based distinguishability as the operative deduplication strategy—but the contradiction turns on whether calling a writer 'safe' is meaningful or a misnomer for 'attaches metadata.' This is REFUTED IF 14e084ed5ca7's own countercondition holds: defining 'safe' broadly as 'attaches metadata that enables downstream deduplication' makes 2edd20cc5e66's layer framing compatible with rather than contradictory to the category-error claim, collapsing the dispute to a terminological one. It is further REFUTED IF 8dc9accbe33c's three-writer counterexample analysis shows the category-error framing cannot distinguish a writer appending random UUIDs per attempt (genuinely unsafe, unidentifiable duplicates) from one attaching consistent delivery IDs (safe under 2edd20cc5e66's definition), since both are indistinguishable to a content-comparison-only replay layer, undermining 14e084ed5ca7's assertion that distinguishability is purely protocol-level and not also an operation property of the writer.
